points.quote: unless specifically required to use AI as part of the assessment submitted work must always be the student’s own writing therefore they must not copy and paste computer generated text directly.
points.gist: Unless the assessment requires AI, submitted work must be the student's own writing, so computer-generated text must not be copied and pasted directly.

points.quote: Students should not use content or ideas from Generative AI without appropriate citation.
points.gist: Students should not use content or ideas from generative AI without appropriate citation.

points.quote: OpenAI. (2022). ChatGPT (Dec 20 version) [Large language model]. https://chat.openai.com/ And a screenshot of the full thread of the cited AI interactions pasted to an Appendix.
points.gist: Gives a reference format example for ChatGPT, with a screenshot of the full AI conversation pasted into an appendix.

points.quote: A general overview use declaration (in the submission declaration) in which you explain in general how technology assistance was used
points.gist: A general use declaration in the submission declaration explains in general how technology assistance was used.

points.quote: Students should not use Generative AI as the first step in their thinking (i.e. to immediately ask the computer the exact question that they have been asked).
points.gist: Students should not use generative AI as the first step in their thinking, such as by asking it the exact assessment question.

points.quote: Students should not input confidential research data, both quantitative and qualitative or copyrighted data/text into an AI tool without approval. If personal data is to be put into an AI tool this must be part of the ethics application process.
points.gist: Confidential research data or copyrighted text should not go into AI tools without approval; personal data must be part of the ethics application.

points.quote: Students should be aware of privacy and GDPR and not input personal and private information about themselves or others.
points.gist: Students should be aware of privacy and GDPR and not input personal and private information about themselves or others.

points.quote: Students should not rely on Generative AI when working in an important context where the student is reliant on the generated output being correct (e.g. legal contexts such as placement risk assessments).
points.gist: Students should not rely on generative AI where correct output is essential, such as legal contexts like placement risk assessments.

points.quote: The use of computer assistance to give the impression that a student has learned more than they have is academic misconduct.
points.gist: Using computer assistance to give the impression of having learned more than one has is academic misconduct.

points.quote: each School of Study should meet at least once per academic year to discuss the impact of generative AI on their assessment design and set School-level expectations around the appropriate use of AI for students within their discipline.
points.gist: Each School should meet at least yearly to discuss AI's impact on assessment design and set School-level expectations for students.

points.quote: Module organisers should make it clear within assessment briefs how Generative AI can be used, ensuring that the policy is adhered to, or where it differs explain why.
points.gist: Module organisers should state in assessment briefs how generative AI can be used, and explain any difference from the policy.

points.quote: UEA has approved the use of the TurnitIn AI detection software for taught programmes, but this must be used with caution by Plagiarism Officers only due to reported inaccuracy
points.gist: Turnitin AI detection is approved for taught programmes but must be used with caution, by Plagiarism Officers only, due to reported inaccuracy.

points.quote: Generation of personalised student feedback on formative and summative assessment. Students can be encouraged to seek ongoing feedback on tasks and assignments, but the justification of a mark should be a human judgement.
points.gist: Staff should not generate personalised student feedback with AI; the justification of a mark should be a human judgement.

points.quote: Students should reflect on AI feedback and other outputs against their own knowledge and understanding and report on the guidance which has been provided and how they may or may not include it in their work.
points.gist: Students should reflect on AI feedback against their own knowledge and report on the guidance given and whether they include it.

points.quote: Students should not circumvent their learning, e.g. when asked to reflect on a task or output from a task.
points.gist: Students should not circumvent their learning, for example when asked to reflect on a task or its output.
